newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich accepts House speakership with apologies.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich accepts House speakership with apologies.

text.p: A chastened Newt Gingrich, narrowly re-elected speaker of the House of Representatives under a cloud of ethical questions, accepted the honour on Tuesday with a blanket apology for any behaviour thay may gave given offence or caused controversy.

"Let me say to the entire House that ... to the degree I was too brash, too self-confident or too pushy, I apologise," Gingrich said in his acceptance speech to the House. "To whatever degree in any way that I have brought controversy or inappropriated attention to the House, I apologise."

"It is my intention to do everything I can to work with every member of this Congress," the conservative Georgia Republican said in an immediate, extended gesture of conciliation to minority Democrats and to the handful of fellow Republicans who refused to support him for re-election.

As its first act upon convening, the new House elected last November voted Gingrich into a second two-year term as its speaker but only after heated controversy over whether he should step aside pending a decision on what punishment he should receive for breach of House ethics rules.

It was widely expected he would be reprimanded for admitting he gave false information to House investigators and for failing to ensure that tax-exempt donations were not used in a college course he taught. Critics say the course involved partisan politcs.

"This has been a very difficult time. Some of this difficulty, frankly, I brought on myself ... and I apologise to the House and to the country for having done so," he said of the ethics contoversy. He was re-elected with a bare voting majority of 216 to 205 for Minority Leader Richard Gephardt of Missouri, a Democrat, and four scattered for other Republicans. Six voted "present," in effect an abstention.
